# Item response models over time

``` r

library(ctsem)
library(ggplot2)
```

A binary item measured repeatedly is an item response model whose latent
ability moves. ctsem fits the two, three and four parameter logistic
forms with `manifesttype = 1`, and the parameters map onto ones already
in the model:

| IRT                   | ctsem                   | notes             |
|:----------------------|:------------------------|:------------------|
| discrimination $`a`$  | `LAMBDA`                | free loading      |
| difficulty $`b`$      | `MANIFESTMEANS`         | enters as $`-ab`$ |
| guessing $`c`$        | `ASYMPTOTES[, 'lower']` | lower asymptote   |
| upper asymptote $`d`$ | `ASYMPTOTES[, 'upper']` | ceiling           |

The two parameter model therefore needs no special arguments.
`ASYMPTOTES` has a row per binary item and a column for each asymptote.
A cell left `NA` means no asymptote on that side, a number between 0 and
1 fixes it, and a name estimates it. Ordinal items are covered in the
measurement models vignette. This one is about binary items and what has
to be fixed to estimate them.

## The response curves

$`P(y=1 \mid \eta) = c + (d-c)\,\text{logit}^{-1}(a(\eta - b))`$. The
three forms differ only in where the curve starts and stops:

``` r

eta <- seq(-4, 4, length.out = 300)
curve3 <- function(a, b, c, d, lab) data.frame(eta = eta, lab = lab,
  p = c + (d - c) / (1 + exp(-a * (eta - b))))

ggplot(rbind(
  curve3(1.5, 0, 0,    1,    '2PL'),
  curve3(1.5, 0, 0.25, 1,    '3PL: guessing 0.25'),
  curve3(1.5, 0, 0.25, 0.9,  '4PL: and a ceiling of 0.9')),
  aes(eta, p, colour = lab)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0, 1), linewidth = .3, colour = 'grey80') +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = 'bottom') +
  labs(x = 'latent ability', y = 'P(correct)', colour = NULL)
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The guessing parameter lifts the floor: someone far below the item’s
difficulty still answers correctly a quarter of the time. The upper
asymptote lowers the ceiling, for items even able people sometimes miss.

## What has to be fixed

The latent process needs a **scale** and a **location**, as in any
factor model, and the logistic link supplies neither. Multiply the
process by $`k`$ and divide every discrimination by $`k`$ and the linear
predictor is unchanged, so the likelihood cannot tell them apart.

There are two equivalent ways to set the scale:

- **fix one loading** at 1 and let `DIFFUSION` be free, or
- **fix `DIFFUSION`** at 1 and let every loading be free.

The latent *variance* cannot be fixed directly, because in continuous
time it is not a parameter. The stationary variance is
$`\text{DIFFUSION}^2/(2|\text{DRIFT}|)`$, a function of two estimated
parameters.

For the location, leave `CINT` and `T0MEANS` at zero and let
`MANIFESTMEANS` hold the difficulties. Freeing both would not be
identified, for the same reason.

`MANIFESTVAR` must be zero, because the logistic link already supplies
the randomness.
[`ctFit()`](https://cdriveraus.github.io/ctsem/reference/ctFit.md) fixes
it to zero if it is left free.

## Simulating and fitting

Ten items with varying discriminations, 250 people, 8 occasions,
guessing at 0.20.

``` r

nitem <- 10
items <- paste0('y', seq_len(nitem))
a <- seq(0.9, 1.9, length.out = nitem)     # discriminations
b <- seq(-1.6, 1.6, length.out = nitem)    # difficulties
guess <- 0.20

gen <- ctModel(type = 'ct', n.latent = 1, n.manifest = nitem,
  manifestNames = items, latentNames = 'eta',
  manifesttype = rep(1, nitem), ASYMPTOTES = c(guess, NA),
  LAMBDA = matrix(a, nitem, 1), MANIFESTMEANS = matrix(-a * b, nitem, 1),
  DRIFT = matrix(-0.4), DIFFUSION = matrix(1.2), T0VAR = matrix(1.342),
  T0MEANS = matrix(0), CINT = matrix(0), MANIFESTVAR = diag(0, nitem),
  Tpoints = 8)

set.seed(7)
d <- data.frame(ctGenerate(gen, n = 250, Tpoints = 8, dtmean = 0.9,
  backend = 'julia'))
```

A length 2 vector, as here, fills every binary item’s row: the lower
asymptote fixed at the guessing probability, and no upper one.

The floor is visible in the data. An item far above someone’s ability is
still answered correctly about `c` of the time, where a 2PL would go to
zero:

``` r

hardest <- d[[items[nitem]]]
ggplot(data.frame(p = c(mean(hardest), guess +
    (1 - guess) * mean(plogis(a[nitem] * (rnorm(1e5, 0, 1.342) - b[nitem]))),
  mean(plogis(a[nitem] * (rnorm(1e5, 0, 1.342) - b[nitem])))),
  lab = factor(c('observed', '3PL expected', '2PL would give'),
    levels = c('observed', '3PL expected', '2PL would give'))),
  aes(lab, p, fill = lab)) +
  geom_col(width = .6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf('%.2f', p)), vjust = -0.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.45)) +
  theme_bw() + labs(x = NULL, y = 'P(correct), hardest item')
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The models differ only in `ASYMPTOTES`. A name in place of a number
estimates that asymptote, and the same name on every item estimates one
guessing parameter for the whole test. A guessing parameter per item is
possible (`cbind(paste0('guess_', items), NA)`) but much harder to
estimate, so a shared one is the usual starting point.

``` r

irtmodel <- function(ASYMPTOTES = NA) {
  m <- ctModel(type = 'ct', n.latent = 1, n.manifest = nitem,
    manifestNames = items, latentNames = 'eta',
    manifesttype = rep(1, nitem), ASYMPTOTES = ASYMPTOTES,
    # Scale: the first loading is fixed at 1 and DIFFUSION is free.
    LAMBDA = matrix(c(1, paste0('a_', items[-1])), nitem, 1),
    # Location: the latent is centred, so MANIFESTMEANS are the difficulties.
    CINT = matrix(0), T0MEANS = matrix(0),
    MANIFESTVAR = diag(0, nitem))
  m$pars$indvarying <- FALSE
  m
}

fit2 <- ctFit(d[, c('id', 'time', items)], irtmodel(),
  backend = 'julia', cores = 1, priors = TRUE)
fit3 <- ctFit(d[, c('id', 'time', items)], irtmodel(c('guess', NA)),
  backend = 'julia', cores = 1, priors = TRUE)
```

``` r

data.frame(model = c('2PL', '3PL'),
  loglik = round(c(fit2$estimate$loglik, fit3$estimate$loglik), 1),
  npars = c(length(fit2$estimate$raw), length(fit3$estimate$raw)),
  guess = c(NA, round(summary(fit3)$popmeans['guess', 'mean'], 3)),
  guess_sd = c(NA, round(summary(fit3)$popmeans['guess', 'sd'], 3)))
#>   model   loglik npars guess guess_sd
#> 1   2PL -11317.6    22    NA       NA
#> 2   3PL -11243.7    23 0.201    0.011
```

The guessing parameter is recovered with a usable standard error, and
the three parameter model fits better for the one extra parameter.

## Reading the dynamics

The reason to fit these models over time is usually the process.
[`ctDiscretePars()`](https://cdriveraus.github.io/ctsem/reference/ctDiscretePars.md)
gives the autoregression of ability across time intervals:

``` r

ctDiscretePars(fit3, times = seq(0, 8, .1), plot = TRUE, indices = 'AR',
  cores = 1)
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Four parameters, and when to stop

Naming the second column estimates the ceiling as well. Both are
reported as probabilities, and either can be estimated without the
other. A ceiling alone, `c(NA, 'ceiling')`, suits items that able people
sometimes get wrong but nobody can guess.

``` r

fit4 <- ctFit(d[, c('id', 'time', items)], irtmodel(c('guess', 'ceiling')),
  backend = 'julia', cores = 1, priors = TRUE)
round(summary(fit4)$popmeans[c('guess', 'ceiling'), ], 3)
#>          mean    sd  2.5%   50% 97.5%  mode
#> guess   0.206 0.011 0.184 0.206 0.228 0.206
#> ceiling 0.986 0.007 0.966 0.988 0.995 0.988
```

These data were generated without a ceiling, so the four parameter model
estimates one that is not there, which is a common situation. Asymptotes
are weakly informed even in cross-sectional item response models with
large samples, and here the dynamics compete for the same information.
Three practical points:

- **Share the asymptote across items** unless you have a reason and the
  data to do otherwise.
- **Use `priors = TRUE`.** The default prior puts the guessing
  probability near 0.18 and the ceiling near 0.95, which is where they
  belong when the data are quiet about them.
- **Check that the fit converged** before reading the estimate. A
  guessing parameter reported without a standard error, or with a
  warning about the curvature, has not been estimated.

## Summary

- A binary indicator with a free loading is a 2PL model. Naming cells of
  `ASYMPTOTES` adds a guessing parameter, a ceiling, or both.
- Fix either one loading or `DIFFUSION` to set the latent scale. The
  stationary variance cannot be fixed directly, since it is
  $`\text{DIFFUSION}^2/(2|\text{DRIFT}|)`$.
- Keep `CINT` and `T0MEANS` at zero so `MANIFESTMEANS` are the
  difficulties, and leave `MANIFESTVAR` at zero.
- Share asymptotes across items and fit with priors. Treat an asymptote
  without a standard error as not estimated.
